subject: NOTAP drift: io/defout.t, op/localref.t, uni/bless.t — perl produces no TAP under the runner; snapshot PCL counts unverifiable
description:
RESOLVED s318: not drift, not unrunnable files — a broken FIXTURE.

Re-run today: all three produce TAP and match the checked-in snapshot EXACTLY —
io/defout.t 22/0 vs 21/1, op/localref.t 64/0 vs 63/1, uni/bless.t 84/0 vs 83/1.
So docs/perl-suite-run.tsv needed no refresh; the rows were right all along.
Two are already blessed XDIFF (io/defout.t = format/$-, op/localref.t = DESTROY
at local-restore). The only UNEXPLAINED row among the three is uni/bless.t t81,
which is task #144 ($! needs the magic-cell box) — already tracked.

CAUSE, reproduced non-destructively: the PERL side runs with CWD = the REAL
$tdir (run-perl-suite.pl:267), so `require './test.pl'` reads perl's own
2069-line harness. In s316v a `cp` followed a symlink out of the shadow and
overwrote it with PCL's 416-line transpilable stub. Real perl then cannot even
COMPILE a test file that says `plan tests => N` (the stub gives `plan` no
prototype) — "syntax error near \"plan tests\"" — so zero TAP, i.e. NOTAP for
every file requiring test.pl. Verified by building a fake t/ with the stub in
place and running perl on io/defout.t: 0 ok lines.

FIXED FORWARD: run-perl-suite.pl now sanity-checks the fixture at startup
(perl's test.pl must exist, contain "most of Test::More functionality", and be
>1000 lines) and DIES with the restore instruction rather than emitting a run
full of NOTAP rows that look like data. NOTAP is labelled "says nothing about
PCL", which is exactly what made the damage quiet. Negative test: pointed the
runner at a fixture with the stub — it dies with the explanation; positive
test: normal run unaffected. Indexed in docs/DECIDED.md §Test/triage infra.</parameter>
</invoke>
